cards.text: This is a psalm of David, for the choirmaster, to be played with flutes. David asks the LORD to give ear to his words and consider his groaning, and he calls Him "my King and my God." Groaning, friend, is not small talk. That's the noise I make lifting a FULL cookie box.

cards.question: David is crying out to his King and his God. When does he say the LORD hears his voice?
True or false: At daybreak, David lays his plea before the LORD and then waits in expectation.

cards.text: Up at daybreak to pray. Friend, at daybreak I'm still LOSING an argument with my snooze button. Then David says something about who God is: He's not a God who delights in wickedness.

cards.question: True or false: David says some evil can still dwell with God.

cards.text: The boastful can't stand in God's presence, David says, and God hates all workers of iniquity. I bragged about my sugar cookies ONE time, and the very next batch came out flat as a coaster.

cards.question: David says the LORD destroys those who tell ___.

cards.text: Then David turns the corner. After all that about who can't come near God, he talks about himself, and he says he WILL enter God's house.

cards.question: David says he will enter God's house. What does he say gets him in?

answers.text: The abundance of God's loving devotion
The long record of his own good deeds
The many offerings he brings to God

cards.question: True or false: David says he will bow down toward God's holy temple in reverence.

cards.text: Now David asks the LORD to lead him in His righteousness, and he says why: because of his enemies.

cards.question: David asks the LORD to make something straight before him. What is it?

cards.text: Make the way straight! Friend, that's MY prayer every time my phone says recalculating. Then David describes his enemies: their throats are open graves, and their tongues practice deceit.

cards.question: True or false: David says most of the words his enemies speak can be trusted.

cards.text: Then David asks God to declare them guilty and let them fall by their own devices. That's a guy who sets a trap and steps right in it on his way out the door.

cards.question: David asks God to drive his enemies out. What reason does he give?

cards.text: Then the psalm turns one more time. David stops talking about his enemies and prays for everyone who takes refuge in God: let them rejoice, let them ever shout for joy.

cards.question: David asks the LORD to ___ those who take refuge in Him.

cards.text: David ends with no maybes at all: the LORD SURELY blesses the righteous, not 'probably' and not 'if the oven cooperates.' Then he gives one last picture, a soldier's picture.

cards.question: In the last line of the psalm, what does David say the LORD surrounds the righteous with?
